# Commands

<!-- Generated by `mise run docs:commands`: this intro from docs/commands-intro.md, the list from the task
descriptions in tasks/*.toml and mise.toml. Edit those, not this file. -->

Every command is a mise task: `mise run <task>`; `mise tasks` lists them. Which to use when:

- **Develop:** `dev`: the real Worker runtime (Intl, board, D1, Durable Objects) on workerd, rebuilt on every save
  with the fast `build:dev`.
- **Build:** `build` is production (what ships and what the tests use), compiled by `WORKER_COMPILER` in mise.toml:
  `tinygo` (smallest wasm, ~1–2 min builds) or `go` (seconds, a bigger wasm, ~50–90 ms slower per request).
  Override it for one run: `WORKER_COMPILER=go ci/check.sh`. `build:dev` is always standard Go, for `dev`.
- **Test:** `check` before pushing (CI runs the same, `ci/check.sh`), then `e2e` for anything in the browser.
  `SMOKE_BASE=https://… smoke` runs the smoke checks against a deployed Worker.
- **Ship:** every pushed branch gets a preview and `main` deploys staging, both automatically (Workers Builds).
  Production: `release v1.3` (or a v* tag from GitHub's Releases page) → CI tests it and tags it → Workers Builds
  deploys it, with no Cloudflare credentials anywhere but Cloudflare. `deploy` does it by hand from a machine with fnox credentials.
  All of them go through `ci/deploy.sh`: [deploy.md](deploy.md).

## Tasks

### `assets`

- Depends: vendor

- **Usage:** `assets`

Tailwind (gsxui CSS) + assemble dist/site (Static Assets for workerd and deploy)

### `bench`

- Depends: build

- **Usage:** `bench`

CPU per request of the production build on local workerd, per page, repeated runs (charter's workerbench)

### `bench:variants`

- Depends: generate, assets

- **Usage:** `bench:variants`

Build the current code with each of charter's optimisations off in turn, measure each, write docs/benchmarks.md

### `build`

- Depends: generate, assets

- **Usage:** `build`

Production build → build/ with WORKER_COMPILER (mise.toml: tinygo or go), size-checked (deploy, staging, CI and the tests use it)

### `build:dev`

- Depends: generate, assets

- **Usage:** `build:dev`

Dev build → build/: standard Go to wasm, seconds after an edit (mise run dev uses it; never deployed)

### `cf:builds`

- **Usage:** `cf:builds`

Set up Workers Builds for $APP_REPO: every branch deploys (previews; production from the production branch), main deploys staging; idempotent

### `deploy`

- Depends: test, token-check

- **Usage:** `deploy`

Test, then deploy production → https://$APP_DOMAIN (or $APP_NAME.&lt;subdomain>.workers.dev), then seo:audit live

### `dev`

- **Usage:** `dev`

gsx dev → build:dev (standard Go, seconds) + CSS → workerd restart on every .gsx/.go save → http://localhost:8913

### `docs:commands`

- **Usage:** `docs:commands`

Regenerate docs/commands.md from these task descriptions (mise generate task-docs); test:go fails when it's stale

### `e2e`

- Depends: build

- **Usage:** `e2e`

Headless Chrome checks: pages, live board in two browsers, boost ↔ board, presence, Intl, write limit (local workerd, or E2E_BASE=https://…)

### `editor:gsx`

- **Usage:** `editor:gsx`

Install go.mod's gsx into GOPATH/bin for the VS Code gsx language server

### `generate`

- Depends: intl

- **Usage:** `generate`

go tool gsx generate (after intl: views write the generated messages); intl/'s own renderer too, which it commits for the apps that import it

### `intl`

- **Usage:** `intl`

Compile the catalogs (intl.toml): the Go package of messages, intl-messages.mjs, the gsxui translator, intl.sum and the languages badge (intl.toml's badge); a language just added to intl.toml's locales gets its catalog. Run it after editing a catalog; gsx generate needs it first

### `intl:check`

- **Usage:** `intl:check`

Every problem, for CI: the catalogs (ICU syntax, arguments, a case for each plural category Intl says a language uses, missing and stale translations, unused messages, gsxui text, intl.sum), then gsx's own checks on the app's markup (gsx generate, gsx fmt, the gsx skill's find-smells.sh); exits 1 on any

### `intl:confirm`

Keep stale translations as they are: the source changed, their meaning didn't (a typo fixed). All of them, or only some: de, or de:board.notes


- **Usage:** `intl:confirm [which]…`

### Arguments
- **`[which]…`** — de, or de:board.notes (default: every stale translation)

### `intl:export`

XLIFF 2.0 per locale into xliff/out (intl.toml's xliff), for human translators and translation-management systems: what is left to translate (--all: every message)


- **Usage:** `intl:export [--all] [locale]…`

### Arguments
- **`[locale]…`** — only these locales (default: all)

### Flags
- **`--all`** — every message, not only what is left

### `intl:import`

Read translators' XLIFF 2.0 back into the catalogs, each target checked against its source: every file in xliff/in, or the ones named; then compile


- **Usage:** `intl:import [file]…`

### Arguments
- **`[file]…`** — &lt;locale>.xlf files (default: all of xliff/)

### `intl:prune`

- **Usage:** `intl:prune`

Remove from every catalog the keys the source no longer has (intl:check names them)

### `intl:skill`

- **Usage:** `intl:skill`

Install or update the intl agent skill (.claude/skills/intl), which Claude Code uses to write and translate the app's text

### `intl:status`

- **Usage:** `intl:status`

Per locale: translated, inherited, stale and missing messages; exits 1 when a locale is incomplete

### `intl:tasks`

- **Usage:** `intl:tasks`

Write this file again from the intl version in go.mod: run it after upgrading intl (intl:check says when)

### `intl:todo`

What is left to translate, per locale: each message's source, context and arguments, the plural categories the language needs, the style note (--json for agents)


- **Usage:** `intl:todo [--json] [locale]…`

### Arguments
- **`[locale]…`** — only these locales (default: all)

### Flags
- **`--json`** — JSON on stdout, for agents

### `intl:translate`

Translate every missing and stale message with Claude Code (the intl skill), one worker per language at once (intl.toml [translate]), until intl:check passes. Needs claude on PATH


- **Usage:** `intl:translate [locale]…`

### Arguments
- **`[locale]…`** — only these locales (default: all)

### `load`

- Depends: build

- **Usage:** `load`

1,000 WebSockets in every locale on one topic, a 50-write burst, socket 1,001 refused (e2e/load; local workerd, or LOAD_BASE=https://…)

### `preview`

Test, then deploy a Worker Preview named after the branch (or e.g. pr-7) → its URL on stdout and in .preview-url


- Depends: test

- **Usage:** `preview [name]`

### Arguments
- **`[name]`** — preview name, e.g. pr-7; the branch unless named

### `release`

Release main to production (e.g. v1.3): CI tests it, tags it, Workers Builds deploys it; no Cloudflare credentials needed


- **Usage:** `release <version>`

### Arguments
- **`<version>`** — the release, e.g. v1.3

### `rename`

- **Usage:** `rename`

Make this template yours: mise run rename -- &lt;module path> &lt;app name>  (e.g. github.com/you/board board)

### `seo:audit`

Fetch robots.txt and every sitemap URL live as Googlebot: 200, indexable, self-canonical, lang, title, description, one h1, reciprocal hreflang (no Google account needed)


- **Usage:** `seo:audit [--json]`

### Flags
- **`--json`** — one JSON document on stdout

### `seo:badges`

- **Usage:** `seo:badges`

Lighthouse on every page and the audit, then the README's badges (seo.toml's [badges] dir: each Lighthouse category's lowest page, the audit) and its &lt;!-- seo:scores --> table; run after a production release, then commit

### `seo:inspect`

One URL (the home page unless named): Google's verdict, last crawl and canonical, and the link to its Search Console page


- Depends: seo:access

- **Usage:** `seo:inspect [--json] [--open] [page]`

### Arguments
- **`[page]`** — a path like /de/ or a full URL

  **Default:** `/`

### Flags
- **`--json`** — one JSON document on stdout
- **`--open`** — open its Search Console page (Test live URL, Request indexing)

### `seo:lighthouse`

Lighthouse on the live site, on Google's servers through PageSpeed Insights: every page of the sitemap (seo.toml's pages), or one; performance, accessibility, best practices and SEO out of 100, what fails and on which elements, real users' Core Web Vitals; fails under seo.toml's min (90)


- **Usage:** `seo:lighthouse [--json] [--desktop] [page]`

### Arguments
- **`[page]`** — one page, a path like /de/board or a full URL; default every page

### Flags
- **`--json`** — one JSON document on stdout
- **`--desktop`** — score the desktop page instead of the mobile one Google indexes

### `seo:setup`

- **Usage:** `seo:setup`

Once: the Google Cloud project, the Search Console and PageSpeed Insights APIs, and a service account key in fnox (needs gcloud auth login)

### `seo:sites`

The Search Console properties the service account can use; fails without Full access


- **Usage:** `seo:sites [--json]`

### Flags
- **`--json`** — one JSON document on stdout

### `seo:skill`

- **Usage:** `seo:skill`

Install or update the seo agent skill (.claude/skills/seo), which Claude Code uses to check and fix how Google sees the site

### `seo:status`

The sitemap's status in Search Console and Google's index status for every URL in it


- Depends: seo:access

- **Usage:** `seo:status [--json]`

### Flags
- **`--json`** — one JSON document on stdout

### `seo:submit`

- Depends: seo:access, seo:audit

- **Usage:** `seo:submit`

Submit https://$APP_DOMAIN/sitemap.xml to Search Console, after access and a passing live audit

### `seo:tasks`

- **Usage:** `seo:tasks`

Write this file again from the seo version in go.mod: run it after upgrading seo

### `seo:todo`

Google's verdict for every sitemap URL (indexed, waiting, duplicate, problem); fails on problems


- Depends: seo:access

- **Usage:** `seo:todo [--json] [--open]`

### Flags
- **`--json`** — one JSON document on stdout
- **`--open`** — open Google's page for each problem (Test live URL, Request indexing)

### `serve`

- Depends: build

- **Usage:** `serve`

The production build (WORKER_COMPILER) on local workerd, static files first → http://localhost:8913

### `smoke`

- Depends: build

- **Usage:** `smoke`

The production build on local workerd, every route checked over HTTP (e2e/smoke); SMOKE_BASE=https://… checks a deployed Worker

### `staging`

- Depends: test

- **Usage:** `staging`

Test, then deploy staging: the Worker $APP_NAME-staging → its URL on stdout and in .staging-url

### `tail`

- **Usage:** `tail`

Stream the deployed Worker's live logs (requests, console, exceptions) → Ctrl-C to stop

### `test`

- Depends: smoke, test:go

- **Usage:** `test`
- **Aliases:** `check`

Everything before a push: the production build + workerd smoke, gsx fmt/gofmt, go vet, go test (mise run check is the same)

### `test:go`

- Depends: generate

- **Usage:** `test:go`

gsx fmt/gofmt check + go vet + go test, the app and intl/ (standard Go; runs beside the production build)

### `token-check`

- **Usage:** `token-check`

Verify CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (from fnox) against the Cloudflare API

### `upstream:branch`

A new branch in an upstream checkout, from upstream's current main


- **Usage:** `upstream:branch <repo> <name>`

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages
- **`<name>`** — the branch, e.g. docs-calendar-from-cldr

### `upstream:check`

An upstream checkout's Go checks with its own pinned Go (gsx generate/fmt, its own check commands, vet, test), no npm; a failing package is re-run on upstream's main and reported as already failing there or new


- **Usage:** `upstream:check <repo>`

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages

### `upstream:fork`

Create your fork of an upstream project on GitHub and add it as the checkout's origin


- **Usage:** `upstream:fork <repo>`

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages

### `upstream:review`

An upstream checkout's commits and diff against upstream's main, to read before anything is sent


- **Usage:** `upstream:review <repo>`

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages

### `upstream:status`

- **Usage:** `upstream:status`

Every upstream checkout (gsx, gsxui, structpages): where it is on disk, its branch, local changes, how your fork's main differs

### `upstream:sync`

Clone or fetch the upstream checkouts (all, or one), adding your fork as origin when you have one; never pushes


- **Usage:** `upstream:sync [repo]`

### Arguments
- **`[repo]`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages (default: all)

### `upstream:tinygo`

An upstream package's own tests compiled by this repo's TinyGo: whether it runs where Workers builds run (e.g. reflect)


- **Usage:** `upstream:tinygo <repo> [package]`

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages
- **`[package]`** — a package pattern in the checkout (default ./...)

### `upstream:unuse`

Back to the pinned version of an upstream project after upstream:use


- **Usage:** `upstream:unuse <repo>`

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages

### `upstream:use`

Build and test this app with an upstream checkout instead of the pinned version (go.work for a Go module; gsxui re-vendored by the checkout's CLI). mise run check fails until upstream:unuse


- **Usage:** `upstream:use <repo>`

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — gsx, gsxui or structpages

### `vendor`

- **Usage:** `vendor`

Vendor htmx 4.0.0 htmx.min.js + ext/hx-ws.js + ext/hx-live.js into web/htmx/ (curl, integrity-checked)
